{{Infobox ancient site|image=File:Tenno-no-mori Kofun, zenkei.jpg|coordinates={{Coord|34.977511|N|135.68965}}|architectural_styles={{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|qid=Q11268718|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}}|part_of={{ill|Otokuni Kofun Cluster|qid=Q123117022}}}}

{{nihongo|{{ill|Tenno-no-Mori Kofun|ja|天皇の杜古墳|my|တန်းနိုးနော့မိုရိခိုဖွန်း|qid=Q28608917|lt=Tenno-no-Mori Kofun}}|[[:ja:天皇の杜古墳|天皇の杜古墳]]}} is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|en|Zenpō-kōen-fun|qid=Q11268718|lt=Zenpō-kōen-fun}} located in {{ill|Misasagi Tsukanokoshi-chō, Nishikyō-ku, Kyoto|ja|京都市西京区御陵塚ノ越町}}, Kyoto Prefecture. It is designated as a National {{ill|Historic site|en|Historic site|qid=Q1081138|lt=Historic site of Japan}}} (as part of the {{ill|Otokuni Kofun Cluster|ja|乙訓古墳群|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135491395}}).

== Overview ==

This tumulus was constructed along the western edge of the {{ill|Kyoto Basin|ja|京都盆地|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10883263}}, near the foothills on the right bank of the {{ill|Katsura River (Yodo River system)|ja|桂川|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2908720}}. Since the medieval period, the mound has been traditionally associated with {{ill|Emperor Montoku|en|Emperor Montoku|qid=Q357225|lt=Emperor Montoku}}, the 55th Emperor of Japan from the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}. The name "Tenno-no-mori" (lit. "Emperor's Forest") and the surrounding area name "Misasagi" (imperial mausoleum) are said to derive from this tradition.<ref name="説明板"/> {{Sfn|Tenno-no-mori Kofun (National Historic Site)|ja|天皇の杜古墳（国指定史跡）}} The mound remains well-preserved, and excavations were conducted between {{ill|1988|en|1988|qid=Q2426|lt=1988}} and {{ill|1989|en|1989|qid=Q2425|lt=1989}}.<ref name="説明板">Site explanation board.</ref>

The tumulus has a distinctive "mirror-handle" keyhole shape with an unexpanded front portion facing south-southeast. The mound is constructed in two tiers.<ref name="説明板"/> {{Sfn|Report on Preservation and Maintenance of Tenno-no-mori Kofun|1994|pp=5-11}} Outer surface features include {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|qid=Q11621213|lt=fukiishi}} and rows of {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|qid=Q849376|lt=haniwa}} (cylindrical and morning glory-shaped).<ref name="京都市"/> {{Sfn|Report on Preservation and Maintenance of Tenno-no-mori Kofun|1994|pp=5-11}} There is no surrounding moat, but remnants of a demarcated area resembling a moat have been identified.<ref name="京都市"/> The burial facility has not been investigated.<ref name="説明板"/>

The tumulus is estimated to have been built in the late {{ill|4th century|en|4th century|qid=Q8099|lt=4th century}} during the early {{ill|Middle Kofun period|ja|古墳時代中期}}.<ref name="京都市"/> {{Sfn|Tenno-no-mori Kofun (National Historic Site)|ja|天皇の杜古墳（国指定史跡）}} Archaeological evidence suggests the individual buried here was a prominent figure who controlled the Katsura River's right bank.<ref name="京都市"/> During this period, the transition from keyhole-shaped to circular mounds is evident in the {{ill|Mukō Hills|ja|向日丘陵}} tombs such as {{ill|Myōkenyama Kofun (Mukō)|ja|妙見山古墳 (向日市)|qid=Q140446117}} and {{ill|Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun|ja|伝高畠陵古墳|lt=Den-Takabatakeryo Kofun}}. However, this site stands out as a large keyhole-shaped tumulus, indicating political importance surpassing the Mukō Hills.<ref name="説明板"/>

The site was designated as a National Historic Site in {{ill|1922|en|1922|qid=Q2165|lt=1922}}, and it has been developed into a public historical park.<ref name="京都市"/>

== Site History ==

* '''1922 (Taishō 11)''': Designated as a National Historic Site.<ref name="国指定">{{National Historic Site Database|401|1638|Otokuni Kofun Cluster}}</ref>
* '''1981-1982 (Shōwa 56-57)''': Public ownership of the surrounding area was established.<ref name="京都市"/> {{Sfn|Report on Preservation and Maintenance of Tenno-no-mori Kofun|1994|pp=5-11}}
* '''1988-1989 (Shōwa 63-Heisei 1)''': Excavations were conducted.<ref name="京都市"/>
* '''1994 (Heisei 6)''': Opening of the historical park.<ref name="京都市"/>
* '''2016 (Heisei 28)''': The National Historic Site "Tenno-no-mori Kofun" was integrated with other tumuli such as {{ill|Igenoyama Kofun|en|Igenoyama Kofun|qid=Q11492427|lt=Igenoyama Kofun}} and {{ill|Terado Ōtsuka Kofun|en|Terado Ōtsuka Kofun|qid=Q11457885|lt=Terado Ōtsuka Kofun}} into the expanded designation "Otokuni Kofun Cluster." Eight additional tumuli were included in this designation.<ref name="告示">March 1, 2016, Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science, and Technology Notification No. 31.</ref> <ref name="文化庁">[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2015112003.html "Regarding Designation of Historic Sites, etc."] (Agency for Cultural Affairs, press release, November 20, 2015).</ref>
